verses.1: I am the man who has seen poverty, struck by the rod of His anger.
verses.2: He has led me and carried me into darkness, and there is no light.
verses.3: Yet He has turned His hand against me all day long.
verses.4: He has worn out my flesh and my skin; He has broken my bones.
verses.5: He has built a wall against me and surrounded my head with a thornbush.
verses.6: He has seated me in darkness like those long dead.
verses.7: He has built a wall behind me; I cannot escape. He has burdened me with a chain.
verses.8: Even if I cry out and beg, He has sealed my prayer.
verses.9: He has built my paths with a wall, and He has made my ways crooked.
verses.10: He is a lion hunting me, a leopard lurking in secret.
verses.11: He has led me in a roundabout way and has thrown me into desolation.
verses.12: He has bent His bow and set me as a target for an arrow.
verses.13: He has driven His arrows into my kidneys, the arrows of His quiver.
verses.14: I have become a laughingstock to all my people; their song through the day.
verses.15: He has filled me with bitterness, made me drunk on gall.
verses.16: He has ground my teeth with gravel, made me swallow ashes.
verses.17: My soul has abandoned peace; I have forgotten what is good.
verses.18: I said, “My strength has perished, and my hope from the LORD.”
verses.19: Remember my affliction and my bitterness, the wormwood and the pain.
verses.20: Remember them, O LORD, and do not let my soul forget.
verses.21: This I will recall to my heart, therefore I will hope.
verses.22: The steadfast love of the LORD is not exhausted, His mercy is not spent.
verses.23: They are renewed each morning; great is Your faithfulness.
verses.24: The LORD is my portion, said my soul, therefore I will hope in Him.
verses.25: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that seeks Him.
verses.26: It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the LORD.
verses.27: It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
verses.28: Let him sit alone in silence, if the burden is upon him.
verses.29: Let him put his face into the dust—perhaps there is hope.
verses.30: Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him, be filled with insults.
verses.31: For the LORD will not reject forever.
verses.32: But with compassion He will have mercy, because of His great steadfast love.
verses.33: For He does not take pleasure in the death of the righteous, nor does He afflict the children of men.
verses.34: To crush all prisoners underfoot, every captive of the earth.
verses.35: To pervert the judgment of a man, to set it before the face of the Most High.
verses.36: To frustrate a man in his cause, the LORD does not see.
verses.37: Who has spoken and it came to be? The LORD has not commanded it.
verses.38: From the mouth of the Most High, neither evil nor good goes forth.
verses.39: Why should a living man complain, a man about his sins?
verses.40: Let us examine our ways, let us search and return to the LORD.
verses.41: Let our hearts lift up their hands to the God in heaven.
verses.42: We have sinned, we have been rebellious, and You have not forgiven.
verses.43: You have covered with anger and pursued us, You have killed and not shown mercy.
verses.44: You have covered with a cloud, so that our prayer cannot pass through.
verses.45: You have made us a disgrace and a mockery among the nations.
verses.46: All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
verses.47: Fear and dread have come to us, the sword and the burning.
verses.48: From the lofty places I will pour down my tears, over the destruction of my daughter, the daughter of my people.
verses.49: My eyes have become dim, they will not be still until the LORD looks from heaven.
verses.50: My eyes are on me from all the daughters of my city.
verses.51: My eyes are weary, my soul is worn out, by the hand of all the daughters of my city.
verses.52: They caught me like a bird, my enemies for no reason.
verses.53: They cut off my life in the pit, laid a stone over me.
verses.54: Water poured over my head, I said, “I am cut off.”
verses.55: I called on Your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit.
verses.56: My voice You heard; do not hide Your ear from my plea, from my cry for help.
verses.57: You came near on the day I called on You, You said, “Do not fear.”
verses.58: You have multiplied the disputes of my soul, You have redeemed my life.
verses.59: You have seen, O LORD, my wrongs; judge my cause.
verses.60: You have seen all their vengeance, all their schemes against me.
verses.61: You have heard their taunts, O LORD, all their schemes against me.
verses.62: The lips of those who rise against me, their thoughts against me all day.
verses.63: Their sitting and their standing, look—watch their eyes.
verses.64: Return to them, O LORD, their deeds, what their hands have done.
verses.65: Give them a heart of stone, Your wrath against them.
verses.66: Pursue them in anger and destroy them from beneath the heavens, O LORD.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 10: "He is a lion hunting me, a leopard in secret" — the Hebrew uses metaphor to describe divine judgment.  
- v. 22-23: "The steadfast love of the LORD is not exhausted, His mercy is not spent. They are renewed each morning" — the Hebrew uses poetic parallelism, which is preserved in the translation.  
- v. 53: "They cut off my life in the pit" — "cut off" is a poetic metaphor for being killed or destroyed.  
- v. 54: "Water poured over my head, I said, 'I am cut off'" — "cut off" is a metaphor for being destroyed or abandoned.  
- v. 64-66: The final verses are a plea for divine justice. The translation preserves the imperative tone and poetic form.
